nodes.title: ABOUT
widgets_values:
# DUGco Animated Path Insert (MiniMax H3)

**Add a creature that crawls across a surface in your shot, and steer where it goes.** The example is a spider climbing a jacket. You draw the route, the route is tracked onto the jacket, and MiniMax H3 paints the spider along it. Everything outside the spider is your original footage.

## How to use
1. **Load your shot** in group 2 (★ Your shot).
2. **Draw the route** in group 3. Run once so frame 1 shows in the ★ Spline Editor, then drag the points: first point is where the creature starts, last point is where it ends.
3. **Set the size and timing** in group 3: ★ Creature size in pixels, and the start and end frame of the move.
4. **Describe the creature** in group 4, and load a reference picture of it.
5. Press **Run**. Group 3 previews the tracked route first; group 6 shows the finished shot and group 7 saves the matte and the creature element for your comp.

## Tips
- **Check the route preview before judging the render.** The orange dot should stay on the cloth for the whole shot. If it slides, raise *anchors* or draw the route over more textured cloth.
- **Direct the actor to the route.** In the example plate she looks down at the spider near the end, although nothing was there on the day. End the route where she is looking.
- **Size matters.** A bigger mask gives H3 more room for legs. Keep it about 1.5x the body you want.
- **New take:** change the ★ Seed in group 5.
- **Up to 15 s per render**, cut to H3's frame grid (17n+5 frames).

## What you need
- **Node packs:** DUGCO Tools (this pack), KJNodes, MaskVidExperiments.
- **Models:** `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot` in `diffusion_models`; `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq` in `text_encoders`; `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16` and `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32` in `vae`; `sam3.1_multiplex_fp16` in `checkpoints`.
- **Example inputs:** `path_insert_plate.mp4` and `path_insert_spider.jpg` from the pack's `example_workflows/inputs` folder, copied into ComfyUI's `input` folder.

## Licence note
**Track Path To Shot downloads CoTracker3 the first time it runs. CoTracker3 is licensed CC-BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial use only.** The rest of this workflow and the DUGCO Tools code are not affected by that licence.

nodes.title: NOTE | Models
widgets_values: **NOTE | Models.** The MiniMax H3 reference-to-video model, its text encoder and the two VAEs. Every other group picks these up by name.

nodes.title: NOTE | Your shot
widgets_values: **NOTE | Your shot.** Load the plate. It is cut to H3's frame grid (the nearest 17n+5 frames at or below its length, up to 15 s). 24 fps footage works best.

nodes.title: NOTE | Animate
widgets_values:
**NOTE | Animate.** 

How the Spline Editor works.

Load your shot in group 2 and press Run once. The editor only shows frame 1 after it has executed, because the frame arrives through its bg_image input.

Drag the points: the first is where the spider starts, the last is where it ends.

Shift+click adds a point at the end, Ctrl+click adds one between two points, and right-click deletes one.

Set the start and end frame on the Track Path To Shot node, and the creature size on the mask node.

nodes.title: ★ Spline Editor: draw the route on frame 1
NOTE | Creature
widgets_values: **NOTE | Creature.** A reference picture on a plain background, and a description of how it moves. Call the picture `<Picture 1>`. Describe the surface it walks on and the light, so it sits in the shot.

nodes.title: ★ Describe the creature and its move
widgets_values: <Picture 1> shows the spider. In the video, one large hairy brown tarantula, exactly the spider in <Picture 1>, crawls slowly and deliberately up the front of the olive-green canvas jacket, climbing from the lower part of the jacket up onto the chest, where it stops and settles, its legs still shifting and feeling the fabric. Its eight jointed legs step one after another in a creeping alternating rhythm, each leg lifting, reaching and gripping the fabric, the heavy body swaying slightly with every step. The spider is seen from above, its back to the camera, pressed against the cloth, casting a small soft contact shadow on the jacket, lit by the same cool soft window light as the scene. The jacket fabric dimples very slightly under its feet. Only one spider. Photorealistic live-action footage, fine hair detail, natural motion blur, film grain matching the shot.

nodes.title: NOTE | Render
widgets_values: **NOTE | Render.** The whole route is cropped out of the shot and enlarged, so the creature gets enough pixels. The crop is encoded, and only the travelling mask is regenerated: H3 sees the real jacket around it and paints the creature into the hole, following your description and picture. *Crop detail* is the working size in megapixels. Change the ★ Seed for another take.

nodes.title: NOTE | Result
widgets_values: **NOTE | Result.** The rendered crop goes back into your shot through a soft copy of the travelling mask, so everything outside the creature is your untouched footage, with its original sound.

nodes.title: NOTE | Comp asset
widgets_values: **NOTE | Comp asset.** For compositing it yourself: SAM 3.1 finds the creature in the finished shot, limited to the travelling mask, and gives a matte. Saved here are the matte as a video and the creature as an RGBA PNG sequence (straight alpha) to layer over your own plate in Nuke, After Effects or Resolve. Change the ★ word to match your creature.
